clue.text: Paper goes on with the motley

blocks.note: first meaning: a large size of writing paper
second meaning: the jester's headgear, put on along with his parti-coloured costume

explanation.walkthrough: Motley is the chequered costume of a court jester; split in two, the answer is the cap that a fool wears with it.
explanation.definitionFit: Foolscap is a traditional British paper size, named for an old watermark showing a jester's hat.

clue.text: Wildly excited when it's put up in foreign currency 1 7).

indicators.note: in a down entry, putting something up lifts its letters so they read from bottom to top
one piece sits inside another, held within the currency

blocks.note: the franc, former currency of France and others
the word it, taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone gets very agitated on discovering their money has been converted into a foreign currency.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray '1 7)' is debris from the newspaper scan. 'Put up' suits a down entry, where letters raised read from the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Frantic describes a state of wild, distraught agitation, exactly the sense of being wildly excited.

clue.text: Hamlet's first part performed thus

blocks.note: surface reading: how the opening section of Shakespeare's tragedy was staged
setter's reading: the first part of the word Hamlet is a ham, a bad actor whose style is exaggerated

explanation.walkthrough: A ham is an actor who hams it up; the way a ham performs is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To overact is to exaggerate a role theatrically, the defining fault of a ham performer.

clue.text: Main support of a bird in Wales

definitions.note: a place in Wales; the clue names its location rather than giving a noun

blocks.note: the swan, a large white water bird
the main is old poetic language for the open sea

explanation.surface: Asking what chiefly sustains some bird found in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry the sea sits beneath the bird and so supports it, as water holds up a floating swan.
explanation.definitionFit: Swansea is a coastal city in south Wales, so the place sits fairly in Wales as the clue demands.

clue.text: Direct speech

blocks.note: first meaning: to mark a letter for delivery, or to aim words at someone
second meaning: a formal talk delivered to an audience

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as the grammar term for quoted words; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: You address an envelope or remarks to someone, and a formal oration is also called an address.

clue.text: Young insignificant member of the jet set?

blocks.note: first meaning: a small, unimportant or cheeky young person
second meaning: a single spurt of liquid, one of a set of jets

explanation.surface: A callow, unimportant youngster mixing among the glamorous international rich.
explanation.walkthrough: The jet set sounds like wealthy travellers; read literally, it is a collection of jets of liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: A squirt is slang for a puny upstart and also a thin stream of water forced out.

clue.text: A job for Adam, rather than for spinster Eve

definitions.text: A job for Adam, rather than for spinster Eve

blocks.clueFragment: A job for Adam, rather than for spinster Eve
blocks.note: surface reading: some task suited to the first man rather than to an unmarried woman
setter's reading: in the old rhyme 'When Adam delved and Eve span', Eve spins while Adam digs

explanation.walkthrough: A spinster was originally a woman who spins thread; Adam's share of the work was digging.
explanation.definitionFit: Spadework is digging with a spade, and by extension the hard preparatory labour on any project.

clue.text: To London with an appointment, to be modernized

blocks.note: one traditionally goes up to London, the capital
having a fixed date, an engagement to meet

explanation.surface: Someone travels to the capital for a meeting, hoping to bring their ideas up to date.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage you go 'up' to London from anywhere else in the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Something updated has been brought into line with current fashion or information, which is modernized.

clue.text: Merrymaking causes revolution on the Spanish lines

blocks.note: rev is short for a revolution of an engine
el is Spanish for the
RY abbreviates railway, a set of lines

explanation.surface: A wild party leads to an uprising along Spanish frontiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Revelry is lively, noisy festivity, the same thing as merrymaking.

clue.text: Queen from Denmark accepts one - hence Cleopatra's Needle 110>.

indicators.note: to accept is to take something in, so the queen's name holds the other piece within it

blocks.note: Queen Alexandra, Danish-born wife of Edward VII
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A Danish-born queen takes one item, the Egyptian obelisk now on London's Embankment.
explanation.walkthrough: The '110>' is scan debris. 'Hence' makes the definition the place the obelisk came from.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleopatra's Needle stood at Alexandria in Egypt before being shipped to London in 1877.

clue.text: Fishy characters met in this low joint?

definitions.text: Fishy characters met in this low joint?

blocks.clueFragment: Fishy characters met in this low joint?
blocks.note: surface reading: shady criminals gather in a seedy bar
setter's reading: fish plunge downwards through the water, and that plunge shares its name with a seedy bar

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fishy' suggests dodgy people, but literally it means fish, who head deep under water.
explanation.definitionFit: A dive is slang for a disreputable bar or club, and also a headlong plunge into water.

clue.text: Such meditation no doubt in Emerson's club

blocks.note: first meaning: the mantra-based practice popularised by the Maharishi
second meaning: the ... Club of New England thinkers, of which Ralph Waldo Emerson was a leader

explanation.walkthrough: Emerson's circle in 1830s Massachusetts called itself after this philosophy.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a TM technique of meditation and the American philosophical movement around Emerson and Thoreau.

clue.text: To ignore a girl is one sort of . weapon

blocks.note: to cut someone is to snub or ignore them
lass is a northern British word for a girl

explanation.surface: Snubbing a young woman is presented as a kind of weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray full stop is scan debris.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutlass is a short curved sword of the kind carried by sailors and pirates.

clue.text: Folds the record she writes to enclose

indicators.note: to enclose is to wrap around, so the writing phrase surrounds the other piece

blocks.note: taken as written
an EP is an extended-play record
to pen is to write

explanation.surface: A woman writes the history of the folds, as in pages or creases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'She writes' gives the outer pair, and the record goes between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A fold is an enclosure for sheep, so folds are pens where a flock is kept.

clue.text: Sounds an excellent bargain - the last word!

indicators.note: sounds says the words are to be heard rather than read, matching by pronunciation

blocks.note: a bargain is a buy, and an excellent one is a good one

explanation.surface: A shopper declares that a fine bargain is the final word on the matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Goodbye is the word said at parting, literally the final thing spoken before someone leaves.

clue.text: North European has one extra supporter in Maryland

blocks.note: a Balt is someone from the Baltic states
the Roman numeral for one
more means additional

explanation.surface: A Latvian or Lithuanian has an additional fan in an American state.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the founding family: Lord Baltimore backed and owned the Maryland colony, and its biggest city carries his title.
explanation.definitionFit: Baltimore is the largest city of Maryland, named after the barons who sponsored the colony's founding.

clue.text: Apply make-up for-show biz - need for some change

indicators.note: a change rearranges things, so these letters are put into a different order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Show business demands that performers put on stage make-up for a change.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 'for-show' is scan debris for 'for show'.
explanation.definitionFit: To bedizen is to dress or adorn gaudily, decking oneself out showily to impress onlookers.

clue.text: Serious art making money

blocks.note: first meaning: sincere and intent
second meaning: in old English, 'thou art making money' is said with the archaic second-person form of earn

explanation.walkthrough: 'Art' is not painting but the old verb form, as in 'thou art'; thou earn'st means you are earning.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest means solemnly sincere, and archaically it is the verb form used with thou for one who earns.

clue.text: Take in mythical old' king in Nice for recreation

indicators.note: re-creation is making anew, so the town's letters are formed again in a new order
one piece placed in another ends up enclosed by it

blocks.note: the French Riviera city, taken as written
King Lud, legendary pre-Roman king of Britain, said to have given his name to London

explanation.surface: A legendary British monarch takes a holiday on the Riviera.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe after 'old' is scan debris. Ludgate in London is named after King Lud.
explanation.definitionFit: To include something is to take it in as part of a whole, to embrace or contain it.

clue.text: Murder's in place with a cooking utensil

indicators.note: 'is in' places one thing within another, so the killing goes inside the place

blocks.note: to set is to place
to kill is to murder

explanation.surface: A crime scene where the weapon is a frying pan.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is short for 'is', telling you the killing sits inside the place.
explanation.definitionFit: A skillet is a frying pan or small long-handled pot used on a stove.

clue.text: Prince's musical role

blocks.note: surface reading: the part a royal heir, or the pop star called Prince, plays in a show
setter's reading: the title part in a 1924 Romberg operetta about a royal who enrols at Heidelberg university

explanation.walkthrough: The Student Prince (1924) is an operetta about a prince who enrols at Heidelberg university.
explanation.definitionFit: In that operetta the prince's role is that of a university undergraduate, hence the title.

clue.text: Showing the mood of Thespian retrospection

definitions.text: Showing the mood of Thespian retrospection

blocks.clueFragment: Showing the mood of Thespian retrospection
blocks.note: surface reading: the feeling an actor has when looking back on a career
setter's reading: John Osborne's 1956 play whose title begins 'Look Back', a theatrical looking back

explanation.walkthrough: Thespian points to the stage and retrospection is looking back, recalling Osborne's play Look Back in Anger.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes someone furious, and it is the last part of a famous play title.

clue.text: Small change once for sunbathers

blocks.note: first meaning: old pre-decimal sixpence coins, called by slang name
second meaning: people who brown their skin in the sun

explanation.walkthrough: A tanner was British slang for a sixpence, a coin withdrawn after decimalisation in 1971.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both old sixpenny coins and people lying out to acquire a suntan.

clue.text: A musical summary about the, surrender

blocks.note: re means about, concerning
capitulation is a surrender; the comma is scan debris

explanation.surface: A tune that sums up the story of a surrender.
explanation.definitionFit: In sonata form the recapitulation restates the main themes, so it is a summary within music.

clue.text: It's hard in the foreign game for the reckless driver

indicators.note: one thing in another sits enclosed inside it

blocks.note: jeu is French for game
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A tough contest abroad suits a dangerous driver.
explanation.walkthrough: In 2 Kings, Jehu 'driveth furiously', so his name became slang for a fast driver.
explanation.definitionFit: Jehu is a humorous old term for a fast, reckless coachman or motorist, after the biblical king.

clue.text: Fast time by this loony flier?

definitions.text: Fast time by this loony flier?

blocks.clueFragment: Fast time by this loony flier?
blocks.note: surface reading: a crazy aviator setting a quick time

blocks.clueFragment: Fast time by this loony flier?
blocks.note: setter's reading: Ember days are church fasting days, and a loon is a diving bird, the great northern diver

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' is abstaining from food, not speed; 'loony' points to the loon, the bird this old name belongs to.
explanation.definitionFit: This hyphenated old name refers to the great northern diver, which Americans call the common loon.

clue.text: City where he escaped the pagans

indicators.note: whatever escaped has got out and is gone, so those letters leave the word

blocks.note: taken as written
heathens are pagans

explanation.surface: A place where a man got away from unbelievers.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the two letters of 'he' away from the start of the word for pagans.
explanation.definitionFit: Athens is the capital of Greece, a famous ancient and modern city.

clue.text: Ways in which a French city appears black as night sometimes

indicators.note: the ways are the setting within which the other piece is found

blocks.note: St is the abbreviation for street, so streets are STS
Arles in Provence

explanation.surface: Streets of a Provençal town look pitch dark at night.
explanation.definitionFit: A starless sky has no visible stars, so an overcast night is completely black.
